summary: 兄弟姐妹的榜样、竞争和父母的偏爱都可能延续到成年后的行为。文章把个案与研究并读，也写到温暖的手足关系怎样帮助孩子关心他人。
logic: 分析比较与偏爱的代价
解释同胞性格为何不同
考察亲密关系带来的帮助

paragraphs.brief: 手足关系为何影响深远
sentences: We can choose our friends, the saying goes, but we cannot choose our family of origin.
俗话说，朋友可以自己选，原生家庭却无法选择。
Our parents provide the genetic material and make powerful early role models, but even more influential in determining what kind of adult we will become are our brothers and sisters — our siblings.
父母把基因传给我们，也是我们早年最重要的榜样，但说到我们将成为什么样的成年人，兄弟姐妹的影响甚至更大。
They occupy a position of unique intimacy in our lives and cast a longer shadow than many recognise or are prepared to acknowledge.
他们与我们格外亲近，影响也比许多人意识到或愿意承认的更深远。
By turns, enraging and lovable, familiar and mysterious, our brothers and sisters are the human beings who people our first social relationships.
兄弟姐妹时而惹人生气，时而讨人喜欢，既熟悉又神秘，也是我们最早交往的人。

And a sibling relationship is the most enduring relationship many of us will ever have — no less emotionally intense than the bonds we form with our spouses and our own children — if only because they started when we were so young.
对许多人来说，手足之情是一生中持续最久的关系，单是因为它从幼年就开始了，而其强烈程度也不亚于我们对伴侣和子女的感情。
paragraphs.gist: 手足与我们一起经历最早的社会关系，其亲密程度和从童年延续一生的时间，使他们对人成年后的影响可能超过父母。

paragraphs.brief: 长子女表现改变教养氛围
sentences: Surprising new research by Dr Gene Brody found that having older children who do well in school and are well liked by other children leads to parental ‘basking’ — increasing mothers’ self-esteem.
吉恩·布罗迪博士的新研究发现，家中较年长的孩子在学校表现好、受同学欢迎，父母也会与有荣焉，母亲的自尊心随之提高。
It is clear that in turn this is associated with more positive parenting of younger children, who display fewer behavioural problems as a result.
这又与更积极地养育年幼子女有关，年幼的孩子因而较少出现行为问题。
Conversely, parents who get a difficult first child may in turn experience a negative spiral of household tension.
反过来，如果头一个孩子就难带，父母可能会陷入恶性循环，家庭气氛越来越紧张。
paragraphs.gist: 研究发现，长子女受欢迎且学业顺利会提升母亲的自尊，改善她对弟妹的教养；头胎难带，则可能使家庭紧张加剧。

sentences: International sports star Piri Weepu is a rugby hard man, but at least some of his tough temperament was forged long ago in the family home.
国际橄榄球明星皮里·威普球风强悍，这种坚韧性格至少有一部分是小时候在家中磨炼出来的。
His older brother Billy started rugby — tackling little Piri when he was just four — to ‘harden him up’.
小皮里才四岁，哥哥比利就开始用橄榄球的擒抱动作对付他，说要让他变得更坚强。
It seemed to work.
看来这招还真管用。
Piri followed his brother in playing for the under-sevens league before he even started school.
皮里还没上学，就跟随哥哥参加了七岁以下儿童的橄榄球联赛。

There are as many such stories as there are families: in the formative hothouse of the family, siblings interact in complex ways with the powerful forcefields of parents, genetics and personality already at work.
几乎每个家庭都有类似的故事：家庭是塑造孩子的地方，兄弟姐妹之间的影响与父母、遗传和个性等因素复杂地交织在一起。
It starts with birth order, which determines play roles: the firstborn leader, the middle-child mediator and the rebellious youngest.
最早起作用的是出生顺序，它影响孩子扮演的角色：老大带头，中间的孩子调解，老幺则常常反叛。
These are roles that can stick for life.
这些角色可能伴随人一生。
paragraphs.gist: 橄榄球星皮里的韧性从小受哥哥磨炼，这个例子引出家庭中排行与个性、遗传和教养相互作用、塑造长期角色的现象。

sentences: Clinical psychologist Claire Cartwright says she has clients who believe, and it might not have been true, that they were treated differently from their siblings, that one child in the family was preferred over others.
临床心理学家克莱尔·卡特赖特说，她的一些来访者相信父母区别对待手足、偏爱其中某个孩子，尽管事实未必如此。
They are quite convinced that the parental judgements on them all those years ago were harsher, and that they were the ones who always got into trouble.
他们深信，小时候父母对自己格外严厉，挨批评的总是自己。
Later, in the workplace, such a person might be particularly defensive, and so behave in a way more prone to attracting harsh judgements.
长大工作以后，他们可能处处戒备，反倒更容易招来严厉的评价。
paragraphs.gist: 童年相信自己受到偏心对待的人，即使记忆未必准确，成年后也可能在职场过度防卫，反而引来更严厉的评价。

paragraphs.brief: 受宠和叛逆的不同后果
sentences: However, the research shows that being Mummy or Daddy’s favourite has its own traps.
不过，研究表明，做父母最宠爱的孩子也有隐患。
If you were the easy-going, co-operative child at home, you probably excelled at pleasing parents and, later, bosses.
小时候若性情随和、凡事配合，你可能很会讨好父母，长大后也很会讨好上司。
But you might, as an adult, find it hard to be assertive with authority figures and lack direction.
但长大后，面对权威人物，你可能难以坚持自己的意见，也缺乏自己的方向。

On the other hand, the sibling who is disruptive and annoying as a child may be able to reinterpret that role later, turning those attention-seeking characteristics into strengths like determination and leadership.
反过来，儿时爱捣乱、招人烦的孩子，长大后可能会把当年博取注意的特质转化为决心和领导力。
paragraphs.gist: 受宠而顺从的孩子长大后可能不善于向权威表达主见，曾经爱惹事的孩子却可能把寻求关注的劲头转化为毅力和领导力。

paragraphs.brief: 同胞经历不同的家庭环境
sentences: How is it that full siblings, despite sharing DNA, can turn out so differently?
同父同母的兄弟姐妹有共同的基因，为什么长大后还能如此不同？
One answer is that, in fact, each sibling grows up in a different family, a unique micro-culture.
一种解释是，每个孩子实际上都成长于不同的家庭环境，各自经历了独特的家庭小文化。
For example, the firstborn is, for a while, an only child, and therefore has a completely different experience of the parents than those born later.
例如，头生的孩子有一段时间是独生子女，因此他们与父母相处的体验跟弟妹全然不同。
The parents themselves are growing up too, weathering hardship or good fortune, so one sibling might experience stability and closeness while another might be raised in the midst of crisis.
父母也在经历成长，有时遭遇困难，有时交上好运，因此一个孩子可能体会到安稳亲密，另一个却是在家庭危机中长大的。
paragraphs.gist: 即使共享遗传背景，长子女曾独享父母的关注，弟妹出生时家庭境况又可能已变，每个孩子实际经历的成长环境并不相同。

paragraphs.brief: 手足互动促进学习与认同
sentences: Of course, there are many positive aspects of sibling relationships.
当然，兄弟姐妹关系有许多积极方面。
Annette Henderson, a lecturer in psychology, says firstborn children learn vocabulary more quickly than their siblings because they are not competing to spend one-on-one time with parents.
心理学讲师安妮特·亨德森说，头生的孩子学词汇比弟妹快，因为他们不必和别的孩子争取与父母单独相处的时间。
But younger children in turn benefit from unintentional instruction from their bigger brothers and sisters, acquiring entire phrases and an understanding of social concepts such as politeness.
弟妹则能从哥哥姐姐无意中的示范里学会完整短语，也能理解礼貌等社交概念。

Similarly, a Cambridge University study of 140 children found that even when there is a great deal of conflict, siblings will still create a rich world of play and make-believe that extends them developmentally.
剑桥大学对140名儿童的研究同样发现，即使经常发生冲突，兄弟姐妹仍会一起创造丰富的游戏与想象世界，促进自身发展。
Love-hate relationships were common among the children, but even those who fought the most had as many positive interactions as the other sibling pairs.
孩子们对手足常常又爱又恨，但即使吵得最凶的手足，积极互动的次数也和其他手足一样多。
It is also true that children compete for parental attention by making themselves different from their brothers and sisters, particularly if they are close in age.
孩子也会让自己与兄弟姐妹有所不同，以争取父母的注意，年龄相近时尤其如此。

A 2003 research paper studied adolescents from 185 families over two years, finding that those who changed to differentiate themselves from their siblings increased the amount of warmth they gained from parents, and also developed stronger personalities and a better sense of their own identity.
2003年发表的一项研究对185个家庭的青少年追踪了两年，发现刻意走出不同于手足的道路的孩子，得到了父母更多关爱，个性也更鲜明，对自我身份的认识更清楚。
paragraphs.gist: 手足带来学习词汇、社交礼貌和想象游戏的机会，即便常吵架也能积极互动，主动与手足区分还有助于形成个人认同。

paragraphs.brief: 小家庭中的亲密与互助
sentences: Another consideration is that many families today are smaller and more intimate than their historical counterparts.
今天许多家庭的规模比过去更小，成员之间也更亲密。

This may be advantageous because siblings tend to know each other better and remain lifelong friends compared to children from bigger or more widely spaced families, who perhaps lose touch with one another after leaving home.
这可能有好处：小家庭的手足往往更了解彼此，更容易成为一辈子的朋友，而孩子多或孩子年龄相差较大的家庭，手足离家后或许会渐渐失去联系。
Then there was a 2010 American study which found that having a sister, whether younger or older, meant that 10- to 14-year-olds were less likely to feel lonely, unloved, self-conscious or fearful.
2010年美国的一项研究还发现，10至14岁的孩子只要有姐妹，无论是姐姐还是妹妹，就较少感到孤独、缺少关爱、局促不安或害怕。
The same study found that having a loving sibling of either gender promoted good deeds, such as helping a neighbour around the house or helping other children at school.
同一研究发现，无论对方是兄弟还是姐妹，只要手足间有爱，就有助于培养善行，例如帮邻居做家务或帮助同学。
paragraphs.gist: 现代小家庭中的手足较易维系亲密关系，研究还发现，有姐妹的青少年较少感到孤独，有亲密手足的孩子也更常帮助他人。

items.en: Parents and siblings play equal roles in shaping people’s adult personalities.
items.zh: 父母和兄弟姐妹在塑造成年人人格方面起着平等的作用。
items.why: 题干说父母和兄弟姐妹作用“equal roles / 同等作用”,但原文明确说兄弟姐妹 even more influential,即影响更大。因此题干与作者观点相反，选 NO。

items.en: People’s first social relationships tend to be with siblings of their own gender.
items.zh: 人们最初建立的社会关系往往是与自己性别相同的手足之间的关系。
items.why: 作者把兄弟姐妹称作最早的社会关系对象，但没有说人最先交往的往往是与自己性别相同的手足。

items.en: People’s relationships with their siblings tend to receive less attention when they marry.
items.zh: 人们与其兄弟姐妹的关系在结婚时往往得不到重视。
items.why: 原文将手足关系的情感强度同婚姻、亲子关系相比。题干问的是结婚前后投入关注是否减少，文中没有这样的时间比较。

items.en: Parental ‘basking’ is advantageous for later siblings.
items.zh: 父母因年长孩子的好表现而感到自豪，这对家中年幼的孩子有利。
items.why: 题干中的 later siblings 对应原文的 younger children。原文说 parental basking 会让父母对年幼孩子更积极，年幼孩子行为问题更少。所以 parental basking 对后出生的孩子有利，选 YES。

groups.label: 观点判断 · YES / NO / NOT GIVEN

items.en: What point does the writer make about birth order in the third paragraph?
items.zh: 作者在第三段如何看待手足的出生排行？
correct: It may shape the characteristics of adults.
出生排行可能塑造一个人成年后的性格。

items.en: What are we told about some of Claire Cartwright’s clients?
items.zh: 文中介绍了克莱尔·卡特赖特的一些来访者的什么情况？
correct: Their perceptions of childhood may be inaccurate.
他们对于童年的看法可能不准确。

items.en: What is the writer’s main point about siblings in the fifth paragraph?
items.zh: 作者在第五段对兄弟姐妹有什么主要看法？
correct: Negative characteristics in children can become positive in adults.
孩子身上被视为负面的特征，长大后可能转化为优点。

items.en: Which of the following best summarises the writer’s argument in the sixth paragraph?
items.zh: 以下哪一种最能概括作者在第六段中的论点？
correct: The family environment may change over time.
家庭环境可能随时间而变化。

items.en: The positive aspects of sibling relationships Annette Henderson suggests that young children’s interactions with older siblings involve ________.
items.zh: 安妮特·亨德森指出，年幼儿童和哥哥姐姐的互动中包含 ________。
items.why: unintentional instruction / 无意中的教导、学会短语和社会概念，概括为 learning experiences / 学习经历。所以 35 选 G。

items.en: Also, a Cambridge study found that siblings still enjoy ________ even when they have a tendency to fight.
items.zh: 剑桥大学的一项研究也发现，即使手足间容易争吵，他们仍然喜欢 ________。
items.why: play and make-believe 对应 imaginative games / 富有想象力的游戏。所以 36 选 B。

items.en: Research conducted in 2003 suggests that children develop ________ as a result of seeking attention.
items.zh: 2003年的研究表明，孩子在争取关注的过程中会逐渐形成 ________。
items.why: differentiate themselves / 让自己区别开来、 stronger personalities, better sense of their own identity 都指向“更强的个体性"。所以37选Fgreaterindividuality。

items.en: Another factor is the trend for smaller families, which may mean today’s siblings enjoy ________ as adults.
items.zh: 家庭规模日渐缩小可能也有影响，这也许意味着如今的兄弟姐妹成年后能拥有 ________。
items.why: 回到对应内容“这可能有好处：小家庭的手足往往更了解彼此，更容易成为一辈子的朋友，而孩子多或孩子年龄相差较大的家庭，手足离家后或许会渐渐失去联系”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: A 2010 American study linked having a sister with ________ among children aged 10–14.
items.zh: 2010年美国的一项研究发现，对于10至14岁的儿童，有姐妹与 ________ 之间存在关联。
items.why: “不太孤独、不觉得没人爱、不那么自我意识过强或害怕”属于心理状态更好，对应 mental well-being / 心理健康、精神幸福感。所以 39 选 K。

items.en: Finally, having a sibling may promote ________ according to the same study.
items.zh: 同一项研究还指出，和兄弟姐妹一起长大可能促进 ________。
items.why: good deeds,如帮助邻居、帮助同学，概括为 generous behaviour / 怀慨、乐于助人的行为。所以 40 选 D。

groups.instructionsZh: 阅读带空格的中译，回想正确词项及其字母。

points: 题干说父母和兄弟姐妹作用“equal roles / 同等作用”,但原文明确说兄弟姐妹 even more influential,即影响更大。因此题干与作者观点相反，选 NO。
good deeds,如帮助邻居、帮助同学，概括为 generous behaviour / 怀慨、乐于助人的行为。所以 40 选 D。
clauses: By turns, enraging and lovable, familiar and mysterious, our brothers and sisters are the human beings ….
“who people our first social relationships”修饰前面的 beings。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 who 时，回看 beings，再把修饰信息接回主句。
And a sibling relationship is the most enduring relationship many of us will ever have — no less emotionally intense than the bonds we form with our spouses and our own children — ….
连接词 if 引出“if only because they started when we were so young”，说明主句的条件关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 if 把这一层关系补进去。
lead: A person’s brothers and sisters can have a powerful effect on their adult behaviour
一个人的兄弟姐妹可以对他们的成人行为产生强大的影响
